_readme: Update manifest for the Spectdrum plugin, fetched by the plugin over raw.githubusercontent.com. This repo holds ONLY this file and release binaries, never source code.
_how_it_works: The plugin shows its update banner only when "version" here is HIGHER than the running build (numeric per-segment compare). While it stays below every shipped build nobody is ever prompted, which is the intended idle state.
_to_publish_an_update: 1) attach the installers to a GitHub Release in THIS repo; 2) point url_win / url_mac at those release assets; 3) only THEN raise "version". Raising it before the files exist prompts every customer to download something that is not there.
_platform_keys: url_win / url_mac are picked by the plugin at compile time; plain "url" is the fallback for either. Until round 142 there was a single url, so a Mac customer would have been handed the Windows .exe.
notes: Every step has its own length as well as its own level: drag the top edge for velocity, the right edge for length, the corner point for both
GENERATIVE mode: each band invents its next pass on its own cycle, at the intensity the dice is set to, and your own pattern is kept as the seed
Spectdrum has its own transport: PLAY and STOP run it with the project stopped, and a tempo lock to open when it should run at a tempo of its own

Four stereo band outputs, so each band can go to its own channel in DAWs that support it, to treat with your own effects (each carries the band itself, without the reverb, the delay or the master section)

Every pattern has its own pitch shift, so one pattern can be transposed while the others stay put. The shifter is a phase vocoder: a bass stays a bass at a half step, every attack comes out once, and MONITOR stays on the project's grid (the plugin reports the engine's latency and the host lines it up)
MONITOR opens the four bands with the sequencer out of the way, and with HOLD any key on your keyboard plays them as a gate
The pattern dice chooses what a roll may change (positions, velocities, lengths), and the roll itself can be driven from your controller

Spectdrum matches its own level to your source, all the time and for any material, so MONITOR, bypass and the pattern sit at the level of what comes in, with no jumps and no clipping. The TRIM knob is now your own offset on top (0 = matched); older presets and projects are converted
MIDI: one CC can drive all four bands together, MONITOR can be learned, and your maps are saved and recalled by name
OSC: TouchOSC or any OSC app can play every step, envelope, pattern and preset, on this computer or from a tablet on your network, and a ready-made TouchOSC surface comes with the plugin
Thirteen new factory presets, 43 in all, and preset menus with folders, type-to-jump, and right-click to rename or delete
ALT-click any knob or slider to type an exact value
Look-ahead is off by default in Preferences, so the plugin adds almost no latency (1.5 ms)

The crackle in the highs is gone: the PEAK ceiling now runs only when the maximizer is in use (AMOUNT up or PEAK lowered) instead of catching every hot source at the defaults; and the per-band resonance rider no longer rides wide bands (it still guards against ringing at high Q)
RESET also opens the frequency lock and turns HOLD off

HOLD and its two settings (restart or follow the clock, tails ring on or cut with the key) are saved with presets and projects, and CUT EVERYTHING now works with a pattern on HOLD as well as in MONITOR
MIX fades linearly between dry and wet (no swell at the centre)
A position roll never leaves a band silent: with one or two steps the dice used to come up empty most of the time, now at least one step always lights

Smaller: undo and redo now step one action at a time and redo is never lost, every destructive confirm button is the same solid red, a host block larger than announced no longer crashes, the pattern-length arrows follow fast clicks and repeat when held, reset confirmations open beside the button you pressed, a preset recalls MONITOR and RESET turns it off, in MONITOR the controls it bypasses go grey, the playing pattern wears its glow colour (white, gold when generative) and the glow stays inside its own space, the analyzer view switches and the dark / light skin stay in step with the TouchOSC surface (switch either in either place), every tap on the surface counts exactly once (a touch screen's doubled tap no longer undoes a toggle) and its WET trim is bipolar like the plug-in's, the TouchOSC surface's pattern slots show a picture of each pattern as the plug-in's do, each instance keeps its own window size, the dry/wet sweep no longer clicks, the frequency lock holds the WET trim, and a preset load leaves your session settings alone
